answer: Agents could earn the right to submit valuable actions only after staking tokens that are slashed when independent audits confirm fraud. A sybil attacker must lock a separate stake for every fake identity, while honest agents risk losing theirs if they endorse fabricated work. This makes identities costly rather than merely numerous: the attacker’s expense rises with the number of agents needed to sway outcomes, and remains exposed until review. The rule can be as clear as a basalt terrace lined with copper markers: each claim has a traceable bond.
